issue_context.title: Scheduler crashes.
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Scheduler went into crash loop.

We upgraded from 1.18 => 1.19 and scheduler started crashing few 100 times and then auto-recovered.

Probably related to this code change - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/65d9f8175844


Seems like we no longer use pointers in HEAD
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107623

1.19 - 1.23 has this bug. Fixed 1.24 onwards.

File corresponding to this crash.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.19.16/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/podtopologyspread/filtering.go#L139

Scheduler not to crash.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* Enable pod topology spread on multiple deployments.
* Do a large deployment - so that `addNominatedPods` gets called.
   ```
  Schedule
  findNodesThatFitPod
  findNodesThatPassFilters
  PodPassesFiltersOnNode
  addNominatedPods
  RunPreFilterExtensionAddPod
  runPreFilterExtensionAddPod
  AddPod
  ```
* Scheduler crashes every few seconds until pending pods drop down to 0.

/sig scheduling

It seems like we can't find the kv pair in `s.TpPairToMatchNum`, do we have new nodes added to the cluster? https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e37e4ab4cc8dcda84f1344dda47a97bb1927d074/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/podtopologyspread/filtering.go#L138

Yes. The nodes are in an autoscaling group. So nodes get added/removed all the time.

We are going to try to apply this patch to see if this avoid the crash from 1.19 - 1.23

```
+               klog.V(1).Infof("hii s.TpPairToMatchNum '%v' pair: '%v'", s.TpPairToMatchNum, pair)
+               if s.TpPairToMatchNum == nil {
+                       klog.V(1).Infof("hii avoided crash pair: '%v'", pair)
+                       continue
+               }
```

Maybe we have to patch like this, I don't think it's because of `s.TpPairToMatchNum` is nil. 
```
if s.TpPairToMatchNum[pair] == nil {
	s.TpPairToMatchNum[pair] = pointer.Int32(0)
}
*s.TpPairToMatchNum[pair] += delta2
```
Yeah make sense.. will try that. Thanks.

```
+               klog.V(1).Infof("hii s.TpPairToMatchNum '%v' pair: '%v'", s.TpPairToMatchNum, pair)
+               if s.TpPairToMatchNum[pair] == nil {
+                       klog.V(1).Infof("hii avoided crash pair: '%v'", pair)
+                       s.TpPairToMatchNum[pair] = new(int32)
+               }
```
Any progress?

Yes it fixed the issue. `s.TpPairToMatchNum[pair]`  being `nil` was the problem.

This could happen as below:
1. We have two pods: P1, P2. P1 is the same as P2 except the pod name
2. We have Node1 fit(nodeAffinity and taint tolerations) for both P1 and P2
3. Try to schedule P1, Node1 is resource exhausted, but P1 preempted successfully.
4. We update Node1 with labels not fit for P2 any more, e.g. P2 is configured with `nodeAffinityNotIn` labelA, then I marked node1 with this labelA.
5. Try to schedule P2, in PodTopologySpread plugin, since Node1 is no longer fit any more, so we skip the calculation of `TpPairToMatchNum `
6. Then we ran to `RunFilterPluginsWithNominatedPods` -> `addNominatedPods` -> `RunPreFilterExtensionAddPod` -> `AddPod` -> `updateWithPod`, we'd like to add nominated pod `P1`, but we don't verify whether `P1` meet the `nodeAffinity` or not, then we'll call `s.TpPairToMatchNum[pair]`, it will return nil. That's the problem
7. In releasev1.24, we changed the field type of `TpPairToMatchNum` to `int`, this problem is buried.
